recipes.name: Pepper-Honey Cedar Plank Salmon
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch salt and pepper to taste

steps.text: Soak cedar planks in warm water for 1 to 2 hours; add a splash of bourbon to water if desired.

Combine honey, soy sauce, pineapple juice, vinegar, lemon juice, and oil in a saucepan; cook over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low. Stir in brown sugar, 1 teaspoon black pepper, cayenne pepper, paprika, and garlic powder; simmer, stirring occasionally, until sauce reduces to a syrupy consistency, about 15 minutes. Set aside.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat. Place planks on the grate. Lightly season salmon with salt and black pepper.

Place fillets onto the planks when they begin to smoke and crackle. Close the grill lid; cook for 10 minutes. Spoon a small amount of sauce over fillets; continue cooking until fillets become opaque, about 5 minutes more. Serve with remaining sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Pepper-Honey Cedar Plank Salmon
raw_recipe.description: This pepper-honey cedar plank salmon recipe features grilled salmon on bourbon-soaked cedar planks and glazes them with a tangy pineapple-soy-honey sauce.

review.reviewBody: Thank you for sharing. This was awesome. Instead of grilling; since we are in apartment, I baked the salmon for 25 min at 350 and it turned out wonderful.

I just want to say that i never ever write reviews. But for this one i had to, because it was so delicious! My husband doesn't really like fish, but i made this dish and he told me it is the best dish that i have ever made! I didn't even use the cedar planks. I cooked the fish on an indoor grill plate for 10 minutes and then for the remaining 5 minutes cooked it in a foil pouch with the sauce on the grill plate. The only thing i changed was that i used rice vinegar instead of white vinegar and it was so good!

I really like this recipe. I made the following alterations (half recipe): substituted orange juice (reduced calorie) for pineapple juice, substituted cider vinegar for white vinegar, left out the cayenne and added 1/4 tsp of salt. I also seared the salmon on one side in olive oil for about 5 minutes. I then removed the salmon from the pan and poured in the sauce in the same pan I cooked the salmon in. I cooked the sauce on medium to medium low for about 10 minutes. I then returned the salmon to the pan, basted the salmon with the sauce and put in the oven for 4 minutes at 375F. The salmon came out perfectly!

I make a recipe from this site almost nightly, and I must say that I think this is in my personal top 3! Unfortunately, I did not have all of the ingredients as specified, so I had to use orange juice instead of pineapple, La Choy Original Sauce & Marinade instead of soy sauce, canola oil instead of olive, and I accidentally doubled the garlic (whoops). Also, I didn't have any cedar planks, so I just tossed everything together pan fried (with a lid on the pan!) the fish on medium heat, seven minutes per side (adding sauce as I went). PERFECTION! And it wasn't too spicy for the hubster.

My boyfriend and I have salmon quite often, so I am always looking for different ways to have salmon outside of the generic Asian sauce, which is what I was afraid this would be at first. It does not now, however taste like a teriyaki or anything like that. It is VERY sweet and has a kick, but the spice was not overwhelming for us. I couldn't distinguish any particular flavors that stood out other than sweet and a little spicy, but it was good. I used half honey and half agave, and I had a hard time thickening it on the stove, so I used a cornstarch slurry and boiled for a few minutes. It thickened up to a beautiful sauce, and the salmon did not need more seasoning than salt and pepper with this sauce. Over all it was good, but only if you like sweet sauces on salmon!

We love this salmon recipe - I thought that I had wrote a review on this before, but apparently I have not. My daughter who hates most fish really enjoyed this recipe. Because I was out of many of the items...I subbed the honey with agave, pineapple juice with orange juice and brown sugar w/ with white sugar and a tbsp of molasses. The cayenne brings a nice heat to the fish. Note....YOU MUST SOAK YOUR CEDAR PLANKS....We were distracted and did not notice that the water had drained...spent about 30 mins straight trying to soak them...needless to say, half way through they caught fire and we had to hose down the BBQ. We removed the fish, put it on a cookie sheet, threw it back on the grill and let it finish...believe me....it had the cedar smoked flavor - haha. GREAT recipe, highly recommend!
Note to self: add fresh ginger and garlic. Delete cayenne, use half honey & half habanero honey.

I made this for the.last Friday of Lent. I did make a couple of small changes: I used coconut brown sugar which has a lower glycemic index, seasoned rice vinegar for the white vinegar (I was out of white) and a 1/2 cup honey (very low on honey and didn’t want to make a trip to the store) . I was awesome! I will be using the sauce for other dishes. In fact, some will be used on the Easter ham today! Love the sweet heat!!!

I liked it a lot. I wanted to lick the bowl with the sauce, it's so tasty. But, I cut down the amount of pepper in this recipe, and used Coconut Aminos as a low salt Soy sauce substitute. I didn't have straight pineapple juice so I opened a can of pineapple chunks in 100% juice and used that. Some of the pineapples got into it, and they were tasty too! 

Like another reviewer, I added more pineapple juice mixed with thickener, because it took way longer than 15 minutes to thicken (like 45 minutes). 

I would've given this 5 stars with the changes I made, but as written, it's 4.

This was our first time grilling salmon on a plank. It sure was amazing how much the plank gave flavor to the salmon. We decided on this sauce because we liked the ingredients of sweet and spice. However I was at the stove top for 45 minutes and the sauce wasn't getting thick like syrup. I followed the instructions to a tee. I had my laptop there and since I had plenty of time to read I saw many reviews complaining about the same problem. Luckily I had a small amount of pineapple juice left and mixed 2T of cornstarch in that and finally my sauce was thickened to the syrup consistency. Once the sauce was thickened it did taste good, a bit on the sweet side with all that honey and sugar. The salmon was tender and moist full of flavor from the plank.

I tried this recipe last night and was very impressed. I have never used cedar planks, so that was an expreience, but loved it. I was temped to merinate the salmon but did not know if it would be 'too much', but followed the recipe as written. Has anyone tried marinating? I did baste it more during cooking rather than just spoon over at the end. The salmon was so moist. I did put burbon in the soaking water for the plank and then rubbed a very small amount of sea salt on the plank.

Thank you for this recipe. I have been making it for years. I started making bowls with the salmon and sauce. Plain unseasoned cooked rice, steamed broccoli, salmon (broken up to bite-size pieces) and sauce then gently mixing it together. It is delicious, thanks to the sauce and salmon.
We make this recipe often and especially when we are trying to impress guests.
Absolutely worth the effort! It just might be the best salmon recipe I've ever tried. The sauce was exquisite and a huge hit.
This sauce is great! Super surprised how well it went with the cedar plank salmon on the grill! Will do this again!
Made it for family on Father's Day, everyone loved it. My sisters usually don't ask to take leftovers of fish, but they did on this one and I had none left over for myself!
Good mix of spices -- flavor was great! Next time I'll reduce the soy by half and maybe do more honey and less brown sugar to help it be a thicker glaze.

I cannot say enough good about this recipe! This recipe is my favorite food, it's my go to for all special occasions. I've made this even for people who say they don't like fish and even they've liked this. The only complaint I could possibly give is that it's too good and that I can't restrain myself whenever it's around. I think one time I ate half of a 3 pound filet of it, and I'm a relatively small person, so that was a lot for me lol. Seriously good recipe here.
I made this recipe just as printed for Labor Day weekend BBQ. Family and friends loved it! This recipe is for sure a keeper. Thank you for sharing. I will definitely make again.
Love this recipe!! The only difference is when I doubled up the ingredients for the sauce so I could use it with shrimp as well I used 1/2 soy and 1/2 teriyaki?. It turned out great!!
